root_cause.text: The madvise_args_are_sane() function in xe_vm_madvise.c fails to validate that the user-supplied pat_index falls within the valid range [0, xe->pat.n_entries) before using it to index into xe->pat.table, enabling an out-of-bounds kernel read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (XE_IOCTL_DBG(xe, args->pat_index.val >= xe->pat.n_entries)) return false;` prior to calling `xe_pat_index_get_coh_mode()`, and the CVE description explicitly states that the validation directly calls `xe_pat_index_get_coh_mode(xe, args->pat_index.val)` without first checking the bounds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary guard and speculation protection for PAT index validation in madvise args sanity check.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check on args->pat_index.val against xe->pat.n_entries and used array_index_nospec() before calling xe_pat_index_get_coh_mode() in the DRM_XE_MEM_RANGE_ATTR_PAT case.
intent_record.how: The change prevents out-of-bounds array access when pat_index.val exceeds the number of PAT entries by returning false from the sanity check. It also uses array_index_nospec() to mitigate Spectre v1 speculation, ensuring that the subsequent coh_mode lookup uses a safe index.
